Desde la pestaña <b>Instalar</b> tienes: From the Install tab you have three ways to get a server, depending on what you already have:
<b>Subir un modpack</b>: si ya tienes un: Upload a modpack: if you already have a modpack downloaded (a .zip, for example exported from CurseForge/Modrinth, or a modpack's “server files”), upload it here and the app unpacks it and gets it ready.
<b>Crear desde cero</b>: arranca desde c: Create from scratch: start from nothing: you choose the Minecraft version, modloader (Forge, NeoForge, Fabric, Quilt or none) and its version, with no mods yet. Useful for modpacks without server files: you create the server with the right modloader and then add the mods by hand.
<b>Buscar y descargar</b>: busca un modp: Search and download: search for a modpack on Modrinth or CurseForge and the app takes care of everything: it downloads the modloader, the mods and the config. Before installing it checks whether that modpack looks like one you already have, so you don't duplicate it by mistake.
En los tres casos eliges también cuánta: In all three cases you also choose how much minimum/maximum RAM (-Xms/-Xmx) the server will have.
Elige un servidor arriba para ver sus pe: Choose a server at the top to see its tabs:
<b>Mods</b>: lista de mods instalados (a: Mods: list of installed mods (enable/disable/delete), upload single mods or a whole folder, and search for new mods online (with version compatibility checks and a warning if it's already installed). The “More options” menu also lets you view possible duplicates, view client-only mods and delete disabled mods in bulk.
<b>server.properties</b>: editor con for: server.properties: a form for the most common settings (difficulty, game mode, whitelist, MOTD…) or plain text for everything else.
<b>Config de mods</b>: edita los archivo: Mod config: edit each mod's config files (config/) from the browser.
<b>KubeJS</b>: si el modpack usa KubeJS,: KubeJS: if the modpack uses KubeJS, manage its scripts (create, edit, move/rename, delete).
<b>Archivos de mundo</b>: crea un mundo: World files: create a new world, switch the active one, or delete the ones you no longer use (except the active one).
<b>Logs</b>: consulta logs rotados y cra: Logs: browse rotated logs and crash reports; if there's a crash, the app tries to identify which mod caused it.
<b>Cambiar versión del modloader</b> (bo: Change modloader version (button in the Mods tab): upgrade or downgrade the modloader without touching mods or the world, warning you first if any mod would stop being compatible.
Desde la pestaña <b>Servidor</b> eliges: From the Server tab you choose which modpack to start (if there's more than one) and whether it accepts connections only from your local network or from any IP.
<b>Consola en vivo</b> — ves el log del: Live console — see the server log in real time and send commands (say, list, stop…) directly.
<b>Chat</b> — la pestaña <b>Chat</b> de: Chat — the console's Chat tab shows only player messages, who joins and leaves, and what's said with say. Whatever you type there reaches everyone as a server message.
<b>Métricas</b> — TPS y MSPT en vivo (ví: Metrics — live TPS and MSPT (over RCON, on Forge/NeoForge) and online players, while the server is running.
<b>Rendimiento</b> — gráficas de TPS, ju: Performance — charts of TPS, players and RAM over the last 24 hours or 7 days. One sample per minute is saved while the server is running; where it was off, the line breaks.
<b>Firewall</b> — controla si el puerto: Firewall — controls whether the Minecraft port is open only on your local network or from outside too (needs administrator permissions).
Gestión global de jugadores, aplicada a: Global player management, applied to every server at once: operators (ops), whitelist, and player or IP bans. If the server is running at that moment, use the console commands so the change takes effect right away (the files alone don't kick or admit anyone live).
Abajo, <b>Estadísticas</b> muestra lo qu: Below, Statistics shows what the world itself records for each player: time played, deaths, mobs, blocks mined, distance travelled… Click a column name to sort by it.
En <b>Modpacks → Copias</b> haces una co: In Modpacks → Backups you make a backup with one click: of the world or full (mods, config, scripts, player lists and the world: restoring it leaves the server exactly as it was). They can be made with the server running (the panel pauses saving for a moment so the backup comes out whole), and then you download, restore or delete them. To restore, the server must be stopped, and a backup of the current state is saved first in case you want to go back. If the disk is running out of space, the panel warns you, and it won't start a backup that won't fit. In Automation you can choose a secondary destination (another disk, a NAS): every backup is duplicated there and, if the one on the main disk is lost, it can be restored from that destination.
El botón <b>Clonar</b> de un modpack cre: A modpack's Clone button creates an identical one (mods, settings, scripts and, if you want, the world) to try changes without touching the good one.
Todo funciona aunque no tengas el panel: Everything works even when the panel isn't open.
<b>Si el servidor se cae</b> — el panel: If the server crashes — the panel restarts it on its own, with a limit on attempts so it doesn't loop if something is wrong. Stopping from the panel or with stop doesn't count as a crash.
<b>Copias automáticas</b> — cada cierto: Automatic backups — every so many hours while the server is running, keeping only the latest ones.
<b>Tareas programadas</b> — reiniciar, p: Scheduled tasks — restart, stop or start a server, run a command or make a backup at a specific time and on specific days. Restarts and stops can warn players beforehand or happen only if nobody is online (if people are, they wait for them to leave, up to the maximum you choose). Try runs it immediately so you can see it works.
Crea cuentas adicionales para otras pers: Create extra accounts for other people you want to be able to use the panel. Only the administrator can create or delete users, and they can't delete themselves.
Edita las variables de entorno (usuario,: Edit the environment variables (username, ports, domain, CurseForge key, auto-update…) and the app's internal tuning numbers (timeouts, limits, page sizes…) straight from the browser. Changes don't apply live: when you save, the panel offers to restart the app right away to apply them (it won't restart if a Minecraft server is running or an operation is in progress).
En <b>Avisos</b> configuras, si quieres,: In Notifications you can, if you want, have the panel message you on Telegram or Discord when the server is ready, crashes, someone joins… Each installation uses its own Telegram bot (you create it with @BotFather) or its own Discord webhook, so notifications only reach you. These changes do apply immediately.

<b>Actualizar modpack</b> (botón de arri: Update modpack (button at the top, next to Clone): moves the server to another version of its Modrinth or CurseForge modpack. It makes a full backup first; the world, server.properties and the player lists aren't touched, the modpack's configuration is overwritten and the mods you added are kept. If the server was installed before the panel saved which modpack it comes from, the first time it asks you to search for it. It keeps going even if you close the dialog or the connection drops.

<b>Paquete para jugadores</b> (en la cab: Player pack (in the modpack header, and in the Server header while it's running) prepares the server's modpack for installing on your computer with the same mods and versions, in CurseForge format (.zip: CurseForge app, Prism, ATLauncher) or Modrinth format (.mrpack: Modrinth App, Prism). If the server is linked to its original modpack, it also includes what the server doesn't use: client-only mods, resource packs, shaders and the modpack's configs. The server's own configs are never included. Limited accounts can prepare and download it too.

<b>Pregenerar</b> (en la cabecera del se: Pregenerate (in the server's header, at the very top) generates the terrain around spawn ahead of time with the Chunky mod, so exploring doesn't force the server to create it on the fly. The first time it offers to install Chunky from Modrinth (it only goes on the server: the player pack doesn't include it) and you can remove it from there too. Before starting it tells you how many chunks it is and how much space they'll take, worked out from what your world's chunks take, and it won't start if they don't fit on the disk. It can run only while the server is empty: it pauses when someone joins, carries on when they leave and also carries on by itself if the server restarts.
